provenance.generatedBy: claude-opus-5-5 · Field Kit v2 Prompt A batch
provenance.notes: Edu family batch. Adult buyers, not parents; many already pay for gym software with a bundled site, so the pitch sits in front of it. Ranges are planning figures, not quotes.

pageStructurePlus.contains: The beginner on-ramp: how many sessions, the barbell lifts and movements it teaches, scaling, the coach-to-athlete attention, and when a newcomer joins regular group classes
pageStructurePlus.why: Nervous beginners worry about getting hurt or looking lost. A clear on-ramp turns 'I'm not fit enough for CrossFit yet' into a booked first session.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Today's workout posted each evening with the movements, the scaled and beginner versions, and the strength piece, archived by date
pageStructurePlus.why: Members check tomorrow's workout before deciding to come, and prospects read a week of workouts to judge whether the gym is for them.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Drop-in fee, which classes visitors can join, the waiver to sign ahead, what to bring, parking, and a gym shirt to buy on the way out
pageStructurePlus.why: Travelling athletes pick a box to drop in at from their phone the night before. A drop-in page turns travellers into paid visits and reviews.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Racks, platforms, rowers, bikes, dumbbell range and specialty bars, open gym hours, key fob or late-night access rules and what members can use unsupervised
pageStructurePlus.why: Lifters and independent trainees join a gym for the equipment and the hours. They want to see the rack count and floor before they visit.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Nutrition coaching, the next six-week challenge dates and entry fee, body composition check-ins, and what members get at the end
pageStructurePlus.why: January and post-summer challenges are how independent gyms sign new members in a batch. The page has to exist before the challenge is announced.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Teen athlete strength and conditioning, masters classes for members over fifty, how coaches scale lifts for age, and the times each runs
pageStructurePlus.why: Parents of teen athletes and older adults both assume a CrossFit gym isn't for them. A dedicated section proves otherwise and fills off-peak hours.

designDirections.name: Whiteboard
designDirections.bestFor: Garage-style boxes and strength gyms that need a free class booking and a daily workout, nothing more
designDirections.headlineSample: CrossFit and barbell classes in {City}. First class free.
designDirections.whyItFits: Redline Mono looks like a timer and a chalk whiteboard, and the type-led hero puts the free class button where the workout would be written.

designDirections.name: Class Grid
designDirections.bestFor: Independent gyms with a full group class timetable, an on-ramp course and open gym
designDirections.headlineSample: Strength training and group classes in {City}
designDirections.whyItFits: Not the family combo: Sky Kite reads as a kids' school, and these buyers are adults. Basalt Lime is built for fitness, dark like a gym floor, with lime CTAs.

designDirections.name: Strength House
designDirections.bestFor: Coach-led strength gyms selling semi-private training and nutrition at a higher monthly rate
designDirections.whyItFits: Navy and brass feel like a members' club rather than a bargain gym, and the serif display signals coaching worth a higher monthly rate.

openers.line: Your gym's Google listing has hours and a phone number but no website, so someone searching a CrossFit gym in {City} can't see the class times or what a first class costs.
openers.hook: Open their Maps listing and confirm there is no Website button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Here's the gym page behind that button: {demo-link}

openers.line: The link on your gym listing opens Instagram, where the class timetable is a highlight from months ago. A newcomer wants the CrossFit schedule and the first-class offer in one place.
openers.hook: Tap the link and find where class times live: a highlight, a pinned post, nowhere. Note it.
openers.linkLine: Your gym's class times and free first class, on one page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your gym's website is the plain page that came with the membership software, with the class list and no coaches, equipment or on-ramp. It books members but doesn't sell the box.
openers.hook: Open the site and check whether it's a software template page. Note one missing thing: coaches, equipment, on-ramp.
openers.linkLine: A gym site that sits in front of your booking system: {demo-link}

openers.line: I opened your gym site on my phone and the class schedule needed sideways scrolling. People check CrossFit class times on their phone in the car before deciding to go.
openers.hook: Only if they have a site. Load it on your phone and note what breaks. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: The same gym, rebuilt for a phone: {demo-link}

openers.line: Booking a free first class at the gym means sending a DM and waiting for a coach to answer between classes. A booking button would take that first visit straight away.
openers.hook: Look for any 'book a free class' or intro form. If it's DM or call only, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A free first class booking for the gym: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your posts of members hitting a deadlift PR or their first pull-up are the best thing the gym shares, and they're gone in a day. A member wins page would keep selling the gym.
openers.hook: Find a recent PR, first pull-up or competition post and note the lift or the member's milestone.
openers.linkLine: Your gym's member wins, kept where newcomers look: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your Google reviews keep mentioning how the coaches scaled workouts for someone nervous about CrossFit. Those reviews belong next to the free class button.
openers.hook: Read their reviews and copy one phrase about coaching or feeling welcome. Quote it if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Gym reviews next to the free class booking: {demo-link}

openers.line: January is when people who've put it off finally search for a gym, and the independent gyms with a free class booking ready take those people before the big chains do.
openers.hook: Use this from November to early January, or August for back-to-routine. Name the moment.
openers.linkLine: A January-ready gym page with a challenge sign-up: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your earliest class starts before the front desk would ever open, and people decide to try a gym late at night. Right now the box only takes a booking when a coach checks DMs.
openers.hook: Check their class times for very early or late classes, and comments asking about times. Note one.
openers.linkLine: A gym page that books the 5am class at midnight: {demo-link}

openers.line: Saw you're looking for a coach for the gym's group classes. Certified coaches look at how a box presents itself online before they apply.
openers.hook: Only if they posted for coaches or front desk. Note the role.
openers.linkLine: A gym page with a coach-with-us section: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your gym is near enough to {Neighborhood} hotels that travelling CrossFit athletes look for a drop-in. They need the fee, the waiver and the class times without messaging.
openers.hook: Check reviews or tags from visitors and whether drop-in info exists anywhere. Note it.
openers.linkLine: A gym drop-in page for visiting athletes: {demo-link}

openers.line: I couldn't find a membership price for the gym anywhere. People comparing an independent gym with the chain down the road want a number before they visit.
openers.hook: Check every page and post for membership rates. If none, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: Gym memberships with prices and what's included: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your coaches' strength and conditioning certifications are the reason to pay more than a chain gym, and they're not anywhere a newcomer would see them.
openers.hook: Look for certifications in coach bios or posts. Never invent one.
openers.linkLine: Your gym coaches and their training, on one page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Sounds like most new members at the gym come in as a friend of a current one. That friend still looks the box up before showing up to class.
openers.hook: Look for 'bring a friend' events or reviews saying 'my friend got me to try it'. Quote it.
openers.linkLine: Where a member's friend would land: {demo-link}

openers.line: That {specific recent job} you posted looked like a great day at the gym. A competition or community workout like that should open the gym's site.
openers.hook: Pick their newest event: an in-house competition, charity workout or lifting meet. Name it exactly.
openers.linkLine: That gym moment, front and centre: {demo-link}

sequence.dm1:
Hi {Owner} — that {specific recent job} you posted looked like a great day in the box.

I looked for a site for {Business Name} and found the listing, the socials and a booking page, but nothing that explains the on-ramp or books a free class. I put together a sample gym site with the class timetable, a foundations course page and a free class booking, with marked placeholders where your photos would go.

Would you like me to send it over?
sequence.dm2:
{Owner} — following up in case my message got buried under member DMs. Here's the sample gym site for {Business Name}: {demo-link}

It has the class grid, a foundations on-ramp page, a daily workout board and a drop-in page, and it hands bookings to the software you already use. If it's not for you, say so and I won't message again.
sequence.call:
"Hi, is this {Owner}? I'm {Your Name}, I build websites for independent gyms and CrossFit boxes here in {City}. I sent you a message a couple of days ago, did it come through?"

IF NO:
"Easy to miss between classes. Short version: I built a sample site for {Business Name} with your class grid, an on-ramp page and a free class booking, with marked placeholders where your photos would go. Can I email you the link?"

IF YES:
"What did you think?"
 → let them talk, don't fill the silence
"The build runs {Build Range}, then {Care Range} a month for hosting and timetable changes. For a gym your size I'd normally quote about {Build Price}. It sits in front of your member software, it doesn't replace it."
"Can I walk you through it for ten minutes in the midday gap between classes?"

CLOSE:
"I'll send a one-page scope and a deposit invoice. We start the day it clears, and it's live before the January rush."

objections.objection: My gym software already gives me a website.
objections.handler: "It runs memberships well. The bundled page lists classes but doesn't sell the on-ramp, the coaches or the equipment. This sits in front and sends sign-ups into that same software."
"Instagram shows the energy. The site is where someone checks the price and books the free class at midnight. It links straight back to the gym's grid."

objections.objection: We don't publish prices. We do a no-sweat intro first.
objections.handler: "Keep the intro. Show a 'memberships from' price and book the intro online. People who arrive already know the gym is in budget, so the intro closes faster."

objections.objection: One of my members built our site.
objections.handler: "Good, keep them involved. I'll hand over the on-ramp and drop-in pages. If they'd rather not maintain it before January, the offer stands."

objections.objection: Summer is dead, I'm not spending.
objections.handler: "Summer is when to build. The January rush starts searching in December, and the free class booking needs to be ranking by then."
"{Build Range}. For you about {Build Price}, because it's the class grid, the on-ramp and a free class booking. A couple of members staying the year cover it."

email.subject: Gym site for {Business Name}

sequence.voicemail: "Hi {Owner}, it's {Your Name}. I build websites for independent gyms in {City}, and I put together a sample one for {Business Name} with a free class booking and an on-ramp page. I'll email you the link. {Your Phone}. Thanks."
sequence.takedown:
{Owner} — I'm taking the {Business Name} gym demo down on Friday to free up the space.

Want me to leave it up? One word is fine either way.
sequence.nurture:
Hi {Owner} — the January gym rush starts searching in December, and a free class booking needs to be live before then. Thought of you.

The site is still here whenever you want it, and nothing's changed on price. {demo-link} if you want another look.

bullets: Peg the build to a couple of members staying the year, never to the cost of a rack or rower.
Price it as a layer in front of their gym software. Don't quote a replacement for billing they already pay for.
The free class or intro booking is its own line. It's the only conversion that matters.
Price the daily workout board as a setup plus a posting habit. If nobody will post it, leave it out.
Keep monthly add-ons under one membership. Owners compare everything to the price of a member.
Sell challenge and January work in October and November, never during the rush itself.

lineItems.item: Free class or no-sweat intro booking
lineItems.description: Max with a waiver signed ahead, goal questions for the coach and handoff into the gym's member software.
Max with session-by-session content, start dates, price and a booking for the first on-ramp session.
Max with scaled versions, a searchable archive and posting from a coach's phone.

lineItems.item: Drop-in visitor page with waiver and fee
lineItems.description: Max with online payment, waiver, class picker and a gym shirt pre-order.
Max with entry payment, team sign-up, check-in dates and a leaderboard page.
Max with a full equipment list, open gym rules and a short walk-through video.
Max when the free class booking, on-ramp, waiver and pricing are all translated.

whatElseYouSell.name: Class-in-action shoot at a busy gym hour
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "One packed evening class shot under real gym light, only members who sign off, gives the box hero shots and a season of posts."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, scheduled at the busiest class of the week with a sign-up sheet for consent.

whatElseYouSell.name: Gym Google profile management
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "The week's workouts, challenges and member wins posted to the gym's Google profile, so people searching for CrossFit nearby see a busy box."

whatElseYouSell.name: Review asks after a member's first month
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Thirty days into membership, when the soreness has turned into pride, new gym members get a short text asking for a review."

whatElseYouSell.name: January and post-summer gym ad campaigns
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Local ads for the gym's free class and nutrition challenge, timed to New Year and back-to-routine in September, paused once intro slots fill."
whatElseYouSell.when: Pitch in October for January and in July for September. Ad spend is on top.

whatElseYouSell.name: Challenge launch kit
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Graphics, an email to past trial visitors and a bring-a-friend offer for the gym's next six-week challenge, all ready the week it's announced."
whatElseYouSell.when: Six weeks before each challenge starts.

whatElseYouSell.name: Gym shirt and wall graphics design
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A member shirt and a wall graphic with a scan code to book a free class, so every shirt worn around town points back to the gym."
whatElseYouSell.when: After launch, timed with a challenge or anniversary.

whatElseYouSell.name: Corporate wellness pitch deck and page
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A page and a short deck for local employers offering group strength training memberships to their staff, built for the gym owner to send."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 4, if they mention employers nearby or lunchtime classes.

whatElseYouSell.name: Monthly gym content calendar
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "You coach, I plan the gym's month of posts around member wins, the workout of the week and challenge deadlines."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 3, if posting falls to whichever coach has time.

withoutAI.route: Physical therapists and chiropractors who treat members
withoutAI.whoPays: The clinic, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The clinic your gym sends sore shoulders to needs a page for lifters and CrossFit athletes. The gym owner's name is the introduction."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Clinics want athletes, and gyms already refer injured members to them. The referral relationship is the sale.

withoutAI.route: Meal prep kitchens that supply the gym fridge
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The meal prep company stocking your gym fridge takes orders by text. I'll build their weekly menu and pickup order page."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Meal prep sells through gyms. The gym owner decides whose meals go in the fridge, so the introduction carries weight.

withoutAI.route: Independent personal trainers renting floor time
withoutAI.whoPays: Each trainer, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The trainers who rent time on your gym floor need their own booking page. I'll build them on a template that names your gym."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Renting trainers live at the gym and see the new site daily. Each one is a small, fast sale.

withoutAI.route: Local race and charity workout organisers
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The charity workout or fun run your gym enters every year still signs people up on paper. I'll build registration and heats."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Organisers lean on gyms for participants and volunteers, and the gym owner's word gets you in.

withoutAI.whoPays: The studio, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The recovery studio your members visit after heavy weeks needs online booking. Your recommendation does the selling."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Recovery studios rely on gym referrals, and owners in fitness know each other.

withoutAI.route: The commercial landlord of the gym's unit
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Warehouse bays like the one your CrossFit box rents sit empty for months with only a sign on the roll-up door. A bay listing page with power, ceiling height and parking would fix that."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Landlords pay to fill bays, and a gym tenant that pays rent and draws traffic is a credible introduction.

withAI.route: Intake request assistant for the physical therapy clinic
withAI.pitchLine: "A lifter describes what hurts and when, and the clinic gets a clean appointment request at any hour instead of a voicemail."
withAI.whyItWorks: It never diagnoses; it collects and books. Clinics lose patients to slow callbacks.

withAI.route: Macro-matched menu helper for meal prep kitchens
withAI.pitchLine: "Customers enter their training goal and the week's meals get suggested from the kitchen's own menu with macros shown."
withAI.whyItWorks: Gym members ask the same 'which meals for cutting' question. Answering it sells bigger weekly orders.

withAI.route: Client booking assistant for floor-renting trainers
withAI.pitchLine: "A trainer's prospects ask about packages and open times, and the assistant answers and books while the trainer coaches."
withAI.whyItWorks: Trainers miss messages mid-session. A low monthly fee is less than one session.

withAI.route: Heat and division assistant for event organisers
withAI.pitchLine: "Athletes ask which division and heat they're in and what the standards are, and the assistant answers from the event rules."
withAI.whyItWorks: Event weeks bury organisers in repeat questions. One event pays for it.

withAI.route: Booking and rebooking assistant for recovery studios
withAI.pitchLine: "Clients ask for a sports massage after leg day and get booked into the next open slot, with a rebook nudge later."
withAI.whyItWorks: Recovery visits are impulsive. Catching the request in the moment is the sale.

withAI.route: Unit enquiry assistant for the landlord
withAI.pitchLine: "Prospective tenants ask about bay size, roll-up doors and power, and the landlord gets a showing request at any hour."
withAI.whyItWorks: Empty bays cost money every month, and tours are easy to count.

softwareAI.name: Free class no-show and follow-up texts
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Someone books a free class at the gym and gets a reminder the night before, then a membership offer the day after their workout."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Day 30. Needs the intro offer, membership options and access to the booking system.

softwareAI.name: Online waiver and drop-in checkout
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Visitors pay the gym's drop-in fee and sign the waiver on their phone before they walk in, so the coach just says hello."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: At build, or the first time a drop-in arrives mid-warm-up. Needs the waiver wording and drop-in fee.

softwareAI.name: PR and lift log for members
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Members log squat, deadlift and benchmark workout results in the gym's own log, and the whiteboard PR wall lives online too."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs the lifts and benchmark workouts they track.

softwareAI.name: Gym DM answerer for prices and class times
softwareAI.pitchLine: "'Do I need to be fit to start CrossFit' and 'how much a month' get an honest answer from the gym's own page, with the free class link."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs the timetable, membership options and on-ramp details. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Attendance drop-off alerts for coaches
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A member who used to train three times a week and hasn't checked in for ten days shows up on the coach's list to message."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs check-in data from their gym software.

softwareAI.name: Workout programming planner
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The head coach plans the month's strength cycle and workouts in one place, and they publish to the daily workout board automatically."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3, once the workout board is live. Needs the coach's current programming notes.

softwareAI.name: Front desk phone assistant for the gym
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Mid-class, with music up, the gym phone still gets answered, the membership question handled and the free class booked."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4, once they trust you. Needs memberships, timetable and booking access. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Nutrition challenge check-in tracker
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Challenge entrants log weekly check-ins and body composition results, and the gym sees a leaderboard instead of a spreadsheet."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Before the next challenge. Needs challenge rules, scoring and dates.

softwareAI.name: Gym review reply writer
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A member reviews their first deadlift PR, and a reply in the head coach's voice is drafted to approve between classes."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2, with the review asks. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Workout caption and post drafts
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Tomorrow's gym workout becomes a short post with the scaled version explained, drafted for the coach to approve each evening."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs the workout board and past captions. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Coach payroll and class count report
softwareAI.pitchLine: "How many classes each gym coach ran, private sessions included, ready for payroll at the end of every pay period."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4, for gyms paying coaches per class. Needs pay rates and class history.

softwareAI.name: Freeze-or-downgrade save flow
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A member trying to cancel their gym membership is offered a freeze or a cheaper plan first. Injuries and busy months often pass."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs the freeze rules and the plans they'll offer.

softwareAI.name: Scaling helper for new members
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A new member asks how to scale today's workout for a sore knee or no pull-up yet, and gets the gym's own scaling rules, never medical advice."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs the coach's written scaling rules and approval of every answer. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Coaching handbook assistant
softwareAI.pitchLine: "New gym coaches check how the box warms up, cues lifts and handles a rowdy class, from the owner's own handbook."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6, for gyms with several coaches. Needs a written handbook and owner sign-off. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Gym retail and supplement shelf ordering
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Members order gym shirts, wraps and protein online for pickup, and the owner sees a reorder list before the shelf empties."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5, if they sell retail. Needs products and prices.

softwareAI.name: Semi-private training booking
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Small-group strength sessions booked and paid as packs, with each coach's open times shown, so the gym sells its highest-margin hour."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5, when they mention adding semi-private. Needs coach availability and pack prices.

softwareAI.name: Former member comeback offer
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Members who left the gym get a note before January and before the next challenge with a comeback offer and the free class link."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs cancelled member history.

softwareAI.name: Member churn risk ranking
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each Monday the gym owner sees which members look likely to quit, ranked from check-ins and billing, with a suggested message."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6, after months of check-in data. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Goal intake summary for coaches
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A free class booking's answers about goals and injuries become a short brief the coach reads before the newcomer walks into the gym."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4, once intro bookings carry goal questions. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Open gym key access log
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Who opened the gym door after hours and when, tied to the member's account, so late-night open gym access stays safe."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6, only for gyms with fob or code entry. Needs the access system's export and member list.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Productise the intro booking and on-ramp pages for independent boxes
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I built a free class booking and on-ramp page that sit in front of one gym's software. Every independent box runs the same software and the same weak page."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Boxes run on a handful of member systems, so one integration serves many gyms. Owners meet at every local throwdown.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "People want a gym with a certified strength coach. A directory tied to your certification records sends them to gyms with your coaches on staff."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Certifiers sell courses on career value. Showing that certification brings gym members helps them sell the next course.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your racks and rigs are in hundreds of garages and boxes. A find-a-gym map of your customers makes your brand the one gym owners recommend."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Equipment suppliers compete on loyalty, and gyms happily appear on a map that sends them members.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Each of your gym locations needs its own timetable, coaches and free class booking on one shared template. I build it once and roll it out."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: One contract becomes several locations, and chains already budget for local pages.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Agency resale of the gym template
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your agency takes gym clients and fights their booking software every time. License my template that already hands off to the common gym systems."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: The software handoff is the hard part, and you've solved it once.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every stop in your fitness competition series needs divisions, heats, standards and live results. One platform for the season, from someone who builds for boxes."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Series run the same format several times a year, and every gym that competes sees the build.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The employer's HR or benefits team, annually
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your staff wellness budget could buy group strength training at local independent gyms. A sign-up page that lists participating gyms makes it simple."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Employers want wellness uptake they can count, and the gym client is the first participating gym.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Strength and conditioning for high school athletics
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The booster club or athletic department, per season
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your teams train off-season at a local gym. A sign-up and waiver page for every team's strength block keeps it organised."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Athletic departments partner with gyms already, and parents need permission forms in one place.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Garage gym and home rig owners
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "The PR log and programming planner built for one gym work for garage gym athletes too, sold as a small yearly subscription."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: The software already exists. Home lifters are a long tail that discovers it through gym members.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Martial arts and boxing gyms in the same industrial parks
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: Each gym, at your normal rate
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "The boxing and grappling gyms in the bays next to your CrossFit box have the same intro-class problem. I work the park unit by unit."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Industrial parks cluster fitness tenants, and the box next door is visible proof.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I work with one barbell gym per neighbourhood in {City}. Owners in other cities get the same intro booking and on-ramp setup with no local conflict."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Non-competing geography lets you reuse the gym template and the finished proof.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Rescue a botched gym software migration
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Switching gym software broke your class links and member sign-ups. I can reconnect the site and the booking flow, because I've done it for another box."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Gyms mid-migration are losing sign-ups daily and will pay to stop it.

upsellLadder.offer: Gym site build plus care plan, one contract
upsellLadder.trigger: They say yes to the demo.
upsellLadder.line: "The gym site and the care plan go on one contract, so a timetable change is a text to me between classes."

upsellLadder.trigger: A drop-in or free class visitor arrives without a waiver signed.
upsellLadder.line: "That visitor filling in a waiver mid-warm-up is exactly what an online gym waiver fixes."

upsellLadder.offer: Free class no-show and follow-up texts
upsellLadder.trigger: A month of free class bookings shows no-shows and visitors who never joined.
upsellLadder.line: "Those free class visitors liked the workout. A reminder and a next-day offer brings more of them back to the gym."

upsellLadder.offer: Review asks after a member's first month
upsellLadder.trigger: The first members who joined through the site hit thirty days.
upsellLadder.line: "New gym members at day thirty are proud and sore. That's when they'll write a review."
